g4ela-30-1-morphology: This is a review of every base in the unit. Port, carry. Tract, pull. Struct, build. Spect, look. Ject, throw. Script, write. Rupt, break. Duct, lead. Form, shape. You know a lot of Latin now. Take a long word apart, and it will tell you what it means.
g4ela-30-2-grammar: Dialogue. Quotation marks go around the exact words. The comma or the end mark goes inside the closing quotation mark. Then the tag: said Trumpkin, cried Edmund. A fast shout can be just a fragment. The marks around it still follow the rules.
g4ela-30-3-spelling: A hard word is usually two or three easy rules stacked up. Hopeful: hope, plus ful, and the e stays because ful starts with a consonant. Take the word apart, use the rules one at a time, and put it back together.
g4ela-30-4-grammar: Editing day, the last one for this book. Check every line of dialogue. Are the exact words inside quotation marks? Is the comma or end mark inside too? Does the tag join with a comma? Fix each one and say why.
